artists.biography: Turin Brakes are a modern English folk duo, comprising Olly Knights and Gale Paridjanian, hailing from Balham, London. They had a UK top 5 hit with their song "Painkiller (Summer Rain)" and are joined on stage by their live band, consisting of Rob Allum and Eddy Myer. Since starting out in 1999, the band have sold around 1 million records internationally. They are currently signed to Cooking Vinyl.

perplexity.description:
Released in 2001, The Optimist LP is the debut studio album by British rock duo Turin Brakes. The album is characterized by its blend of acoustic-driven melodies, gentle harmonies, and introspective lyrics, drawing from influences in folk, indie rock, and Britpop. Tracks like "Underdog (Save Me)," "The Door," and "Feeling" showcase the band’s signature sound—warm, melodic guitar work paired with emotive vocals, creating an atmosphere that is both intimate and expansive.

As the first full-length release in Turin Brakes’ discography, The Optimist LP established the band’s reputation for thoughtful songwriting and subtle musical craftsmanship. The album was well-received by critics and earned a nomination for the prestigious Mercury Prize in 2001, highlighting its significance in the UK music scene at the time. Though released on the Source label, its enduring appeal has led to continued recognition and reissues, including by Two Piers, Two Piers. Commercially, the album helped launch Turin Brakes’ career, setting the tone for their subsequent work in the rock genre.
